editorial.headline: Wildlife Sanctuaries: Conservation Management with a Clear PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the stewardship of wildlife sanctuaries where species, habitats and ecosystems are protected and allowed to develop naturally.
editorial.body:
A wildlife sanctuary is not simply a place where animals are present. This activity concerns managing a nature-reserve area distinguished by the diversity or uniqueness of its animal life, while supporting the habitat on which that life depends. Its setting may also be defined by distinctive plants, fauna and ecosystems, or by a particular protected ecosystem whose development proceeds naturally. The scope is therefore conservation management in its fullest sense: protecting the character of the area while maintaining the conditions that sustain it.

The record frames the activity around the management of the sanctuary itself, rather than around a separate commercial service or a particular type of operator. It does not specify any business-scale tier open to the activity. That absence matters: the record supports a reading of the conservation function and its ownership position, but it does not assign the activity to a listed scale category.

At the national level, the PMA position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full shareholding limit nationally for this activity. That is the starting point, but it is not a substitute for reading the Bali position on its own terms. Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium applies island-wide to all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is identified in Bali as Medium-High or High risk, so it is not blocked by that moratorium.

That makes the Bali conclusion more direct than a blanket warning, but not casual. The record calls for verification by address. A foreign investor considering a wildlife-sanctuary activity in Bali therefore has an open national PMA route and no moratorium block on the stated risk basis, while the proposed location still requires address-specific confirmation. The governing distinction is not whether conservation activity sounds sensitive in the abstract, but the status and risk treatment recorded for this particular activity.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor has an open national PMA route here, but the proposed Bali address still requires confirmation.
